title: Turbopuffer Pricing: All Plans Compared (2026)
summary: Turbopuffer pricing bases charges on storage, writes and queries, with each plan setting a monthly minimum you'll need to budget for before integration.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Turbopuffer Costs and Limits That Affect Pricing


Beyond the headline rates, four things move a turbopuffer bill. They're how queries are metered, the limits your data shape runs into, whether a query hits cold or warm data, and the embedding spend that never appears on its invoice.


Each one decides where your 10x total lands relative to the minimum.


### Billing units and per-request minimums


Because queries are metered by data queried, each one is billed for at least 1.28 GB. A small namespace therefore costs the same per query as a 1.28 GB one, so a chatty app with tiny indexes pays for volume it never touches.


Above that floor, marginal discounts apply: 80% above 32 GB and 96% above 128 GB queried, so the per-unit cost of additional queries plummets above 128 GB.


Large, mostly idle data gets cheaper per gigabyte as it grows, which is the shape of workload the pricing favours.


If your data is small, pinning is not an option: it keeps a namespace warm on dedicated capacity and carries a minimum of 64 to 128 GB as of August 2026.


Committed-spend discounts are the other lever, but they only pay off if your monthly usage reliably clears the commitment.


Hit a limit on namespace size, document count or attributes and you have to change your data layout rather than pay more, because these are fixed ceilings, not price tiers.


Check them before choosing between one namespace per tenant and a shared namespace with a filter, because that choice sets both your per-query minimums and your ceiling.


### Cold queries and cache behaviour


Whether the data is in cache decides latency. The[turbopuffer performance documentation](https://turbopuffer.com/docs/performance.md) puts p50 between 14 and 874 milliseconds, p90 between 17 and 1214, and p99 between 27 and 1686, spanning warm to cold.


874 ms cold against 14 ms warm is roughly 60 times at p50, so an interactive search box that sits idle overnight will feel slow on the first query of the morning.


Constant-hot workloads stay near the low end but pay for that constant traffic. Idle data is cheap, but it's slow to wake.


### Costs outside turbopuffer: embeddings and sync


Turbopuffer will not create your vectors for you; it stores and searches them. **Every document and every query needs an embedding** from a model provider, billed separately per token. For a team re-embedding after a model change, **that charge can exceed the storage bill** .


Once you keep the index in sync with your source database, that adds its own cost: each upsert is a metered write, and the job that runs it is infrastructure you operate.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can run that job, and the run is the meter: its published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, however many steps, so a ten-step sync of fetch, filter, embed, batch and upsert costs the same as the two-step shortcut it replaced.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so splitting the job into smaller, more reliable steps raises the charge there, while turbopuffer meters the same writes either way.
